purpose: Triage table for agents: decide from this file alone which units to open and which to skip. One entry per skill, project, research page and tool. Checked by skills/validate_skills.py (every entry path exists, every skills/* and projects/* directory and research page has an entry, every entry is named in README.md).

units.read_when: every coding-agent session in one of the owner's repositories, before inspecting the repo
units.skip_when: never; it is the always-on layer

units.read_when: the repository's real build entry point is a CMakeLists.txt that calls find_package(Qt6 ...) or qt_add_executable, or the task names Qt, QWidget, QML, moc, QProcess, QTest, windeployqt
units.skip_when: no Qt 6 CMake target in the repo (Lua mods, PyQt, .NET, web, scripts)

units.read_when: the task is in the gifscythe repository, or you are calibrating the Qt skill or qt_lint against a real tree

units.stack: Lua 5.1 / LuaJIT mod for the SUGAR engine
units.read_when: the task is in the shotgun-king-anew repository, or you need the executed example of REA process capture + obligation ledger around a mod test harness
units.skip_when: any other repository and any task that is not about mod safety or REA

units.stack: Python / Bash — free-API AI team kit (in-repo, not a pointer)
units.read_when: the task is the AI team kit: quota-aware free-provider pool, adaptive council/Odysseus direction, model scout, or harness code/docs

units.stack: KoboldCpp on Google Colab (adapted official notebook; replacement not yet owner-run on Colab)
units.read_when: the task involves running KoboldCpp on Colab as a pooled API endpoint for the AI team, the test notebook, or its direct Colab link
units.skip_when: any other project; do not treat the endpoint as relied-on infrastructure until W-021 terms evidence exists

units.read_when: choosing tooling or a route for modding a game, or deciding whether a lua-game-modding lane is worth building
units.skip_when: the task is not about game modding or reverse engineering

units.read_when: deciding where skills live, composing the process layer with a writing register, or extending the owner's skills-repo compiler
units.skip_when: the task is inside a project and does not touch skill packaging

units.read_when: the task is the magnet-excavator tool itself
units.skip_when: everything else; it shares nothing with the skills or projects

units.read_when: installing the skills into a harness (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Copilot, Qwen Code, Cursor, Qwen Chat) or adding a harness profile: which ones load real skill directories, which read files by path, which are paste-only
units.skip_when: inside-project work; the question is not about harness installation
